claimsToVerify: Many Roman working-class apartment residents lacked kitchens and relied on street stalls/thermopolia.
Thermopolia had embedded terracotta jars (dolia) in masonry counters.
Romans consumed snails fattened on milk as described in ancient culinary accounts.
Garum was made from salted fish viscera fermented in the sun.
Upper-class Roman literature depicted popinae and thermopolia as disreputable hubs for low-status individuals.
